root_cause: payment-service answers far slower than its callers allow: responses exceed the 2 s budget checkout-service gives it, so calls toward it time out while the rest of the system stays healthy

evidence.supports: payment-service response time is the thing that changed

evidence.observation: 694 timeouts toward payment-service, each carrying timeout_s=2.0
evidence.supports: the responses exceed the 2 s budget - a p95 of 4.85 s sits well above it
the failures are confined to that one dependency
the other dependency barely moved - the slowdown sits in payment-service, not in the caller

evidence.observation: stayed at 0.0 for the whole window
evidence.supports: nothing queues on checkout-service's database pool

ruled_out: CPU saturation in checkout-service - p95_by_dependency[payment-service] rose x50.02 while p95_by_dependency[inventory-service] rose only x1.67; a CPU-bound caller slows both by comparable factors
connection pool exhaustion - db_pool_usage stayed at 0.0 throughout

an internal error in a dependency - dependency_failures[inventory-service] stayed at 0.0 and dependency_error appears once with status=409; the 694 failures are dependency_timeout events, not error responses
memory leak - memory_mb went 89.4 to 99.6 and cache_entries stayed at 0, both among the metrics that stayed normal
